newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page-April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page-April 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 28:
PHILADELPHIA - President Bill Clinton, urging Americans to volunteer in their communities, joined two of his predecessors to help clean up a graffiti-smeared neighborhood.
WASHINGTON - D.C. Police arrested a suspect in the fatal shooting of an off-duty officer near his police station.
WASHINGTON - A growing number of soldiers are facing felony criminal charges for love affairs that in civilian life would break no laws as the Pentagon cracks down on adultery and related offenses.
WASHINGTON - The National Weather Service, which tracks the nation's weather patterns, is facing a $41 million budget shortfall and plans to abolish about 200 jobs.
WASHINGTON - Television-as-we-know-it is about to change after the federal government opened the door for a new kind of broadcasting -- digital broadcasting -- earlier this month.

BERLIN - Germany has tightened its borders, but may ease naturalization for generations of resident "foreigners," the guest workers who began migrating from Italy, Greece and Turkey nearly four decades ago.
